stimuli.text: A solid insulating sphere of radius R = 0.19 m has a total charge Q = +5 nC distributed uniformly throughout its volume.
An initially uncharged 13 µF capacitor, a 10 kΩ resistor, an ideal 13 V battery and an open switch are connected in series. The switch is closed at t = 0.
Students measure the resistance of different lengths of a wire with a diameter of 0.4 mm, using a battery, an ammeter and a voltmeter.

A conducting rod of mass 0.7 kg and length 0.8 m slides without friction on horizontal rails connected by a 5 Ω resistor. A uniform 0.8 T magnetic field points vertically through the rails. The rod is given an initial speed of 3 m/s and then released.

questions.stem: The current in a wire is $$I(t) = 3t^2$$ A. How much charge passes a point from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 5$$ s?
A proton moves at $$8 \times 10^{5}$$ m/s perpendicular to a uniform 0.12 T magnetic field. What is the radius of its path?

options.why: Correct. qvB = mv²/r, so r = mv/(qB).

questions.stem: A 46 µF capacitor is charged to 45 V. How much energy does it store?
A long straight wire carries a uniform charge of 1 µC/m. What is the field 0.41 m from it?

options.why: Correct. E = λ/(2πε₀r), from Gauss's law with a cylinder.
A line charge's field falls off as 1/r.

questions.stem: Two identical small conducting spheres carry 9 µC and -8 µC. They are touched together and separated. What is the charge on each?

options.why: The total is shared between two spheres.
Add the charges with their signs.
Correct. Identical conductors share the total charge equally.

questions.explanation: Total 1 µC, split equally: 0.5 µC each.

questions.stem: A 60-turn coil of area 0.04 m² is perpendicular to a magnetic field that changes by 0.6 T in 0.8 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: Multiply by the number of turns.

questions.stem: A 10 µF capacitor is in parallel with a series combination of 7 µF and 9 µF. What is the equivalent capacitance?

options.why: The series and parallel rules are swapped (they are the reverse of resistors).
Not all the capacitors are in parallel.
Correct. Capacitors add in parallel; reciprocals add in series.
Not all the capacitors are in series.

questions.stem: A 37 Ω resistor is connected across 35 V. What power does it dissipate?
A solenoid 0.7 m long has 500 turns and carries 7 A. What is the magnetic field inside it?

options.why: Correct. B = μ₀nI with n = N/L.
That resembles a wire's field; use B = μ₀nI.

questions.stem: A long straight wire carries 18 A. What is the magnetic field 0.16 m from it?

options.why: That is the field at the center of a loop.
A long wire's field falls off as 1/r.

questions.stem: Two point charges of 8 µC and −9 µC are 0.31 m apart. What is the magnitude of the force between them?
How much work must an external agent do to move a +4 µC charge slowly from a point at 66 V to a point at 123 V?
A flat circular coil of 31 turns and radius 0.2 m carries 7 A. What is the field at its center?

options.why: That is a straight wire's field.

questions.stem: Point P is 0.1 m from a +8 µC charge and 0.6 m from a −4 µC charge. What is the electric potential at P?

options.why: The negative charge contributes negative potential.
Correct. Potential is a scalar: add kq/r with signs.

questions.stem: A 0.5 m wire carrying 16 A makes a 30° angle with a uniform 0.3 T magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force on it?

options.why: Use sin θ, from the cross product.

questions.stem: A wire 5 m long has a diameter of 0.9 mm and resistivity $$2.8 \times 10^{-8}$$ Ω·m. What is its resistance?

options.why: Correct. R = ρL/A with A = π(d/2)².

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor has plates of area 0.16 m² separated by 1 mm, filled with a dielectric of κ = 3.5. What is its capacitance?
The current in a 0.27 H inductor changes by 7 A in 0.16 s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf?

options.why: That is power from energy; use ε = L dI/dt.

questions.stem: A 4 µF capacitor starts uncharged and is charged through a 130 kΩ resistor by a 14 V battery. What is the capacitor's voltage after 1.56 s?

options.why: Convert kΩ and µF to Ω and F.
Correct. τ = RC = 0.52 s; V = ε(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
The change is exponential, not linear.
That is the charging resistor's voltage.

questions.stem: A battery with emf 20 V and internal resistance 0.3 Ω is connected to a 7 Ω resistor. What is the terminal voltage?

options.why: That is the internal voltage drop.
Correct. I = ε/(R + r); V = ε − Ir.
Some voltage is lost across the internal resistance.

questions.stem: Two long parallel wires 0.16 m apart carry 10 A and 2 A in opposite directions. What is the force per meter between them?

options.why: Correct. F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πd); antiparallel currents repel.
The force per length falls off as 1/d.
Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel.

questions.stem: A single loop contains a 11 V battery and a 5 V battery connected so their emfs oppose each other, plus resistors of 7 Ω and 5 Ω. What is the current?

options.why: Both resistors are in the loop.
Correct. Loop rule: ε₁ − ε₂ − I(R₁ + R₂) = 0.

questions.stem: How much work must an external agent do to move a +1 µC charge slowly from a point at 38 V to a point at -2 V?
Two parallel plates 0.08 m apart have a potential difference of 90 V. What is the field between them?

options.why: Correct. In a uniform field, E = ΔV/d.

questions.stem: A 4 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 9 Ω and 10 Ω, connected to an ideal 18 V battery. What is the equivalent resistance?

options.why: R₂ and R₃ are in parallel.
Correct. Reduce the parallel pair, add the series resistor, then work back.

questions.stem: A solid insulating sphere of radius 0.08 m has 8 µC distributed uniformly through its volume. What is the field magnitude 0.24 m from its center?

options.why: Correct. Outside, the sphere acts like a point charge.
Outside, all the charge is enclosed.
Use the distance from the center, r.

questions.stem: Charges of 2 µC, 3 µC, 5 µC sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle with sides 0.4 m. What is the system's electric potential energy?

options.why: Keep the signs of the charges.
Correct. Add kqᵢqⱼ/r for all three pairs.

questions.stem: A ring of radius 0.09 m carries 3 µC spread uniformly. What is the field magnitude on its axis 0.24 m from the center?

options.why: Only the axial components add; the others cancel.
The charge is not at the center.

questions.stem: A 0.6 m conducting rod slides at 10 m/s along rails connected by a 15 Ω resistor, perpendicular to a uniform 1 T field. What is the induced current?

options.why: Correct. ε = BLv, I = ε/R, F = ILB = B²L²v/R.
That is the emf, in volts.

questions.stem: An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of 1000 V. What is its final speed? ($$m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31}$$ kg)
A uniform field of 800 N/C passes through a flat 0.9 m² surface whose normal makes 60° with the field. What is the flux through the surface?

options.why: θ is measured from the normal, so use cos θ.

questions.stem: An ideal 19 V battery is connected at $$t = 0$$ to a 1 Ω resistor and a 1.7 H inductor in series. What is the current at $$t = 3.4$$ s?

options.why: Correct. τ = L/R = 1.7 s; I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−t/τ)).
The current has not reached its final value.

questions.stem: A conducting sphere of radius 2 cm carrying 30 nC is connected by a long thin wire to an uncharged conducting sphere of radius 4 cm far away. What charge ends up on the smaller sphere?

options.why: Equal potential gives Q ∝ R, not R².
Correct. Connected spheres reach equal potential, so Q ∝ R.
That is the larger sphere's charge.

questions.explanation: kQ₁/R₁ = kQ₂/R₂ with Q₁ + Q₂ = 30: Q₁ = 10 nC.

questions.stem: A charge of +16q is at $$x = 0$$ and a charge of +q is at $$x = 7$$ m. At what point between them is the electric field zero?

options.why: The zero point is closer to the smaller charge.
Compare r², so take square roots.

questions.stem: Charges of +8 µC and +6 µC are 1 m apart. What is the magnitude of the electric field at the midpoint between them?

options.why: Each charge is d/2 from the midpoint.
The distance is d/2, so r² = d²/4.
Check the directions of the two fields at the midpoint.
Correct. Like charges' fields point in opposite directions at the midpoint: subtract.

questions.explanation: Each field is k q/(d/2)²: 2.88 \times 10^{5} and 2.16 \times 10^{5} N/C, opposite, giving 7.19 \times 10^{4} N/C.

questions.stem: The electric potential along the x-axis is $$V(x) = 90x^2$$ V. What is the x-component of the electric field at $$x = 0.5$$ m?
A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and remains connected to the battery. A dielectric with κ = 2 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's charge?

options.why: Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.
Correct. With the battery connected, V is fixed and C rises by κ.
Inserting the dielectric changes the capacitance.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. V fixed: Q = CV and U = ½CV² rise by κ.

questions.stem: A 17 µF capacitor charged to 14 V discharges through a 50 kΩ resistor. What is the capacitor's voltage after 0.425 s?

options.why: Correct. τ = RC = 0.85 s; V = V₀e^(−t/τ).
Convert kΩ and µF to Ω and F.
The change is exponential, not linear.

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. A dielectric with κ = 5 is inserted to fill the gap. What happens to the capacitor's charge?

options.why: Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Each quantity changes by at most a factor of κ.
Decide first whether Q or V is held fixed.
Correct. Disconnected, Q is fixed and C rises by κ.

questions.explanation: C becomes κC. Q fixed: V = Q/C and U = Q²/(2C) fall by κ.

questions.stem: An LC circuit has a 6 mH inductor and a 24 µF capacitor. What is its angular frequency ω of oscillation?

parts.prompt: Using Gauss's law, derive expressions for the electric field magnitude inside (r < R) and outside (r > R) the sphere.

rubric.criterion: Spherical Gaussian surface; enclosed charge inside is Q(r/R)³.

parts.prompt: Calculate the field magnitude at r = 0.095 m and at r = 0.38 m.
Sketch (describe) a graph of E versus r from 0 to 3R.

rubric.criterion: Linear increase from 0 to a maximum at R, then 1/r² decrease.
rubric.example: Peak value kQ/R² = 1250 N/C at r = R.

parts.prompt: Calculate the electric potential at the surface and at the center (V = 0 at infinity).

rubric.criterion: Center potential by integrating the inside field.

parts.prompt: Write the loop equation for the circuit and solve it to find q(t).
Calculate the time constant, the initial current and the final charge on the capacitor.
Sketch (describe) graphs of the capacitor's voltage and the current versus time.

rubric.criterion: Capacitor voltage rises from 0 toward ε, concave down.
Current decays exponentially from I₀ toward 0.
rubric.example: About 37% of I₀ at t = τ.

parts.prompt: Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor after a long time, and compare it with the energy supplied by the battery.

rubric.criterion: The battery supplies Qε, twice as much; half is dissipated in the resistor.

parts.prompt: Describe (draw) how the ammeter and voltmeter should be connected, and how R is determined.

rubric.criterion: Ammeter in series with the wire; voltmeter in parallel across it.
Keep the current small or brief so the wire does not heat up.

parts.prompt: Plot (describe) R versus L and draw a best-fit line. Calculate its slope.
Use the slope to calculate the resistivity of the wire.

rubric.criterion: Uses slope = ρ/A with A = π(d/2)².

parts.prompt: The students then use a wire of the same material with twice the diameter. Predict the new slope of R versus L and explain.

rubric.criterion: The slope becomes one quarter as large because the area quadruples.

questions.title: A sliding rod in a magnetic field

parts.prompt: Describe qualitatively how the rod's speed changes after it is released, and explain using Lenz's law.

rubric.criterion: The rod slows down, approaching zero.
rubric.example: Its speed decreases ever more slowly.

rubric.criterion: The induced current produces a magnetic force opposing the motion (Lenz's law).
rubric.example: The force opposes the change in flux.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the magnetic force on the rod in terms of B, L, v and R.

rubric.criterion: Uses ε = BLv and I = ε/R.

parts.prompt: Write and solve a differential equation for v(t).
Calculate the initial current, and explain where the rod's initial kinetic energy ends up.

rubric.criterion: All of the kinetic energy is dissipated as thermal energy in the resistor.
